Multiplies the rate at which NPCs recognize targets that step into their field of view.\n \nHigher values (e.g., 2.0x) make NPCs spot enemies much faster. Lower values give the player more time to duck back into cover before being fully detected.

The percentage of magazine capacity remaining before an NPC decides to retreat, take cover, or stop shooting to reload.\n \nLowering this (e.g. 0.2 = 20%) makes NPCs more aggressive and likely to empty their magazines before falling back.

The maximum angle (in radians) an NPC must be turned toward their target before they begin firing.
 
Values Reference:
 - 0.17 (10 deg)
 - 0.35 (20 deg)
 - 0.39 (22.5 deg - Default)
 - 0.52 (30 deg)
 - 0.70 (40 deg)
 - 1.04 (60 deg)
 - 1.57 (90 deg)
 
Higher values make NPCs much more reactive, allowing them to "spray and pray" while turning instead of waiting to be perfectly aligned.

Controls how long an NPC "sticks" to their current NPC target before being allowed to switch to a different NPC.\n \nHigh values prevent NPCs from rapidly switching targets in large squad battles (flickering behavior). Low values make them extremely reactive to new threats from other NPCs.

Controls the delay before an NPC can switch their focus from another target to the Player.\n \nSetting this to 0 (default) means NPCs will drop everything to shoot the player the moment they are detected. Increasing this gives the player a "grace period" if the NPC is already busy fighting someone else.

Controls how long an NPC remains focused on the Player before they are willing to switch to a different threat (like a mutant or another NPC).\n \nHigh values make NPCs "obsessed" with the player, ignoring other enemies until the player is dead or hidden for a long time. Low values allow them to be easily distracted by other fights.

Sets the duration an NPC will remain in the "Search/Ambush" state after losing visual contact with a target.\n \nHigh values (default 15s) make NPCs stay alert and camp corners or cover for a long time. Low values make them give up quickly and return to idle/patrol states sooner.

The minimum base time an NPC will hold their position in combat before deciding to move, flank, or retreat.
 
Default: 1000. 
 
Lower values make NPCs reconsider their tactical position much faster, resulting in more dynamic and less static firefights.

A random amount of time added on top of the base inertia to make NPC hold times unpredictable.
 
Default: 2000. 
 
Lower values make NPCs more consistently aggressive, while higher values introduce more variation (some will push fast, others will hold longer).

The base inertia time (in milliseconds) it takes an NPC to throw a grenade when the target is close (under 15m).
 
Default: 1000. 
 
Lower values make grenade throws significantly faster, reducing the time NPCs stand exposed.

The additional delay added for each 15m distance threshold (e.g. 15-30m, 30-45m, 45m+).
 
Default: 500. 
 
This simulates the extra time needed to aim and wind up a longer throw.

The inertia time required for an NPC to aim their weapon before firing.
 
Default: 500. 
 
Lower values allow NPCs to shoulder their weapon and fire much faster.

The delay between burst shots when an NPC is firing.
 
Default: 300. 
 
Lower values make NPC burst fire significantly faster.
How long NPCs keep firing at an enemy's last known position after losing sight.\n \nDefault: 10000. Set to 0 to fire only while the enemy is visible.
Extra distance beyond the weapon's pick distance where suppression fire still makes sense.\n \nDefault: 2.5.
Maximum vertical difference between an NPC and its enemy where firing still makes sense.\n \nDefault: 2.0.
Minimum weapon pick distance required for the NPC to consider firing sensible.\n \nDefault: 2.5.
Radius marked as dangerous when an NPC is shot while using cover.\n \nDefault: 3.0.
How long cover remains marked as dangerous after an NPC is shot there.\n \nDefault: 120000.
Radius marked as dangerous when an NPC chooses a flanking detour.\n \nDefault: 5.0.
How long a cover area remains marked as dangerous after a flanking detour.\n \nDefault: 120000.
Cover danger-zone radius created for an unknown threat.\n \nDefault: 5.0.
How long an unknown-threat cover danger zone remains active.\n \nDefault: 120000.
Radius used by the first cover-search pass.\n \nDefault: 10.0.
Radius used by the fallback cover-search pass when nearby cover is unsuitable.\n \nDefault: 30.0.

Maximum preferred cover distance for NPCs using shotguns.\n \nDefault: 5.0.
Minimum preferred cover distance for NPCs using sniper weapons.\n \nDefault: 20.0. Set to 0 to disable the minimum.

How long an NPC waits at smart cover before giving up on it.\n \nDefault: 30000.

Calls Lua GC repeatedly on separate thread with parameters below to collect garbage while engine is rendering frame

How much data to collect in a single call. RECOMMENDATION: in order to hit the sweet spot when frame time is flat and Parallel GC doesn't thrash CPU, type "lua_parallel_gc_debug 1" in the console and check memory usage. It should stay flat at a given value, usually about 45-50MB. To INCREASE efficiency of Parallel GC, FIRST increase GC Step, THEN increase amount of calls. If you think you can afford less aggressive GC, to DECREASE it, FIRST decrease amount, THEN GC Step. Prioritize higher GC Step than Call Amount to reduce overhead on accessing Lua. Default values are very good for vanilla (might run even lower values) and good for Gamma

How much calls to perform to collect garbage. This amount is NOT guaranteed if frames are rendered too fast. RECOMMENDATION: in order to hit the sweet spot when frame time is flat and Parallel GC doesn't thrash CPU, type "lua_parallel_gc_debug 1" in the console and check memory usage. It should stay flat at a given value, usually about 45-50MB. To INCREASE efficiency of Parallel GC, FIRST increase GC Step, THEN increase amount of calls. If you think you can afford less aggressive GC, to DECREASE it, FIRST decrease amount, THEN GC Step. Prioritize higher GC Step than Call Amount to reduce overhead on accessing Lua. Default values are very good for vanilla (might run even lower values) and good for Gamma
